raw_response:
I'm 65 this year, been farming these same 13 mu since I was 25. Never went to school, can't read those papers the extension office hands out, but I know this land better than any book. It's just me and my wife now—the children work in Shijiazhuang or somewhere, send a little money at Spring Festival but not enough to live on. We have to make do with what the land gives us.

This year, same as last year and every year I can remember: wheat then maize, all 13 mu. I don't try new things anymore. At my age, change is just another way to lose money. Last year the wheat gave about 800 jin per mu, the maize about 900 jin per mu. Not great, not terrible. Enough to eat and sell a bit.

For the wheat, I plant around October 10th to 15th, when the air turns cold and the cotton farmers are done harvesting. I keep some seed from last year, good sturdy stuff, but I buy a little to refresh—costs about 50 yuan per mu. Before planting, I spread the base fertilizer. I bought five big bags of compound fertilizer for the wheat. That's not quite half a bag per mu, but close. Then in spring, when the wheat starts turning yellow at jointing time, I topdress with urea—four bags total for the 13 mu. Lao Wang down the road uses more, but he has a bigger farm and his son helps with money. I use what I can afford. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat doesn't dry out, once at jointing in March, and once when the heads flower. Pumping costs about 18 to 20 yuan each time per mu. I watch the sky—if it rains good I might skip one, but last spring was dry so I'll probably do all three.

Maize goes in right after we cut the wheat, around June 8th to 12th. The window is tight, sometimes only five or six days. I hire a few days of help for planting because I can't do it all fast enough at my age. Hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. Fertilizer at planting: five bags of compound spread in the rows, then three bags of urea topdress when the corn is knee-high. Irrigate twice—once if it's dry right after planting, once at the big trumpet stage. I spray herbicide for both crops, and insecticide if I see worms. Costs about 25 yuan per mu for wheat, 20 for maize.

For labor, my wife and I do most of it—about 10 days for wheat, 8 days for maize between us. But I hire 5 days of help for the busy times around wheat harvest and maize planting, and another 4 days for maize harvest. Hired hands want 120 yuan a day now. Everything adds up.

Total cost this year will be around 6,700 yuan. That's a big chunk of what we have. I expect about 800 jin per mu of wheat and 900 jin per mu of maize if the weather holds. If prices don't drop, we should be alright. But I'm not buying more fertilizer than this—I need to keep some cash in hand for my wife's medicine and for pumping water if the drought gets worse.
